issues.reason: The obliques rule fixes the head as the word actually used and forbids a synonym head for a near-fit reading ('in stays In'), and the text says 'ways TO end', not 'for' — the surface-faithful head is available, so the substitution is not forced by the gap.
Same head substitution on the second conjunct, and the same rule governs it.

gaps_confirmed: A noun with a to-infinitival complement ('ways to end world hunger'): the noun-complement section covers of-phrases and prepositional arguments, and the purpose head To is defined between two events, so nothing squarely licenses an infinitival complement on a noun's own symbol.

A bare indefinite plural in object position carrying its own modifier ('discuss ways to ...'): the bare class symbol is reserved for non-specific objects and group witnesses are minted for definite/counted plurals, leaving no settled form.
new_gaps: The infinitive marker 'to' is not a preposition, so the entity-attached surface-head convention does not strictly cover it; whether an entity-first (To <noun> <event>) is the same head as the event-to-event purpose connective To is unspecified.
repair_summary: Replaced the substituted head For with the surface word To in both noun-complement atoms (ways1_for1, ways1_for2), keeping the entity-attached-oblique shape, the reified-but-unasserted end events and every other atom unchanged.
notes: The end events correctly carry class and Patient with no tense, so nothing claims the ending occurred; proof names were left as-is to keep the diff minimal.
